title: Partition Labels
statement: Split the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part. Return the sizes of the parts in order.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(52)
    return [''.join(r.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz') for _ in range(100000))]

hints.1_question: A part must at least extend to the last occurrence of every letter inside it. How can you find those last occurrences quickly?
hints.2_nudge: Precompute the last index of each letter. Scan left to right keeping the farthest last-index needed; when i reaches it, the part can be cut.
hints.3_big_hint: last = {c: i}. end = max(end, last[c]) at each step; if i == end: record end - start + 1 and set start = i + 1.

known_bugs.name: only extends the part by the first letter's last index
known_bugs.followup: In 'abab', a's last index is 2 but b occurs at 3. Is cutting after index 2 allowed?

known_bugs.name: replaces the end instead of taking the max
known_bugs.followup: A later letter may have an earlier last index than the one you already needed. Should that shrink your end?

known_bugs.name: rescans the whole string for each letter's last index (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: How many characters do you scan to find one letter's last position? Could you compute all of them once?

followups: Why is the greedy cut at the first possible place optimal?
How is this related to merging intervals?
